summary: Specifies new Name Type values for the ICMPv6 Trust Anchor option in SEcure Neighbor Discovery, based on certificate Subject Key Identifiers. It updates RFC 3971.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds ways for SEND's Trust Anchor option to identify certificates using Subject Key Identifier hashes. It also updates how new Name Type values can be registered.

questions: what is the send trust anchor option
what is a subject key identifier
what are send name type values
subtitle: New SEND Trust Anchor name types based on certificate Subject Key Identifiers.

tldr.problem: Certificate subject names are unique only within a CA, while SEND needs a way to identify trust anchors across CAs.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines Name Type values 3 through 7 for SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 SKI identifiers.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 3971's Name Type registration procedure and adds identifiers based on SKIs.

today: RFC 6495 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3971. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: Why Use Subject Key Identifiers
sections.content:
SEND uses certificates to certify a router's authority over an IPv6 prefix. The Trust Anchor option identifies the selected trust anchor, and RFC 3971 defined X.501 name and FQDN forms.

A certificate subject name is unique only within a certification authority. The certificate profile used for SEND makes the Subject field meaningless and requires the Subject Key Identifier extension, so this RFC adds SKI-based name types.
sections.plainLanguage: A name alone may not distinguish certificates from different authorities. The new forms use an identifier derived from the certificate's key.

sections.title: The New Name Type Values
sections.content:
Name Type 3 identifies a SHA-1 SKI; 4, 5, 6, and 7 identify SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 SKIs. Values 0 and 255 are reserved, while 253-254 are for experimental use.

Type 3 contains a 160-bit SHA-1 hash of the DER-encoded ASN.1 bit string of the subject public key. Implementations MAY support the defined SKI name types.
sections.plainLanguage: The name-type number identifies which hash is used. Some values are reserved, and two values are set aside for experiments.

sections.title: Router Processing and Registry
sections.content:
If the Trust Anchor option uses an SKI, the value MUST equal the certificate's X.509 SKI extension. A router SHOULD include the Trust Anchor option in the advertisement associated with the certification path it found.

IANA updated the registry and changed its registration procedure to Standards Action or IESG Approval. The security section notes that duplicate identifiers in a validation path can cause the router to stop fetching certificates and SEND validation to fail.
sections.plainLanguage: The router checks the option's SKI against the certificate. The registry now lists the new values and the updated approval process.
